text_content:
The team behind Next.js has created a React hook library for data fetching called [https://swr.vercel.app/](https://swr.vercel.app/). It is highly recommended if you are fetching data on the client-side. It handles caching, revalidation, focus tracking, refetching on intervals, and more.
Using the same example as above, we can now use SWR to fetch the profile data. SWR will automatically cache the data for us and will revalidate the data if it becomes stale.
For more information on using SWR, check out the [https://swr.vercel.app/docs/getting-started](https://swr.vercel.app/docs/getting-started).

Data Fetching
description: Next.js allows you to fetch data in multiple ways, with pre-rendering, server-side rendering or static-site generation, and incremental static regeneration. Learn how to manage your application data in Next.js.
text_content:
Data fetching in Next.js allows you to render your content in different ways, depending on your application's use case. These include pre-rendering with **Server-side Rendering** or **Static Generation**, and updating or creating content at runtime with **Incremental Static Regeneration**.

Examples - [AMP](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/amp)
With Next.js you can turn any React page into an AMP page, with minimal config, and without leaving React. You can read more about AMP in the official [amp.dev](https://amp.dev/) site. ## Enabling AMP To enable AMP support for a page, and to learn more about the different AMP configs, read the [API documentation for `next/amp`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/configuring/amp). ## Caveats - Only CSS-in-JS is supported. [CSS Modules](/docs/pages/building-your-application/styling) aren't supported by AMP pages at the moment. You can [contribute CSS Modules support to Next.js](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/10549). ## Adding AMP Components The AMP community provides [many components](https://amp.dev/documentation/components/) to make AMP pages more interactive. title: AMP - AMP Validation
text_content:
AMP pages are automatically validated with [https://www.npmjs.com/package/amphtml-validator](https://www.npmjs.com/package/amphtml-validator) during development. Errors and warnings will appear in the terminal where you started Next.js.
Pages are also validated during [/docs/pages/building-your-application/deploying/static-exports](/docs/pages/building-your-application/deploying/static-exports) and any warnings / errors will be printed to the terminal. Any AMP errors will cause the export to exit with status code `` because the export is not valid AMP.
